question: Is there an Executive (or executive position) who champions data and analytics or innovation? (This might include a Chief Data Officer, Chief Analytics Officer, or BICC Executive Sponsor or similar titles).

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Organisation structure siloed to focus on localised efforts
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Organisation structure supports targeted enterprise needs and initiatives
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business structure supports most enterprise needs & localised efforts
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Business organised to deliver and considers operational and broader strategic needs
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Business structure adapts to change whilst providing high quality operations

question: Do your Executives get the data and analytic results that they need?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Access to less than half the analytics outputs that are required.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Access to some of the analytics outputs though missing key components.  Value prop measured at silo-level, not overall
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Access to most of the analytics outputs
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Access to all data required but analytics are mostly retrospective or time-delayed
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analytics outputs received in real-time and alerts in place on event triggers

question: How effectively is data and analytics used to support business processes?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No analytics are in use.  Decisions are based on gut-feel and historical data
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Analytics are occasionally used to advise on strategic decisions
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Analytics are available for most decisions and are sometimes used to over-ride gut feel decisions
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Most strategic and tactical decisions are based on analytic outcomes, and some operational decisions are automated based on analytic models
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analytics drives operational and strategic value differentiation from the market

question: Does your organisation have an "Analytics as a Service" function (either internally or contracted externally) where analytics skills (ranging from report developers through to data scientists) are available on call to assist in delivering business outcomes?

How do senior executives communicate the vision and goals? Are their direct reports and their organizations aware of the enterprise vision and goals?  Are their direct reports and their organizations aware of areas specific vision and goals and how those support the enterprise?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is little or no communication of the analytics vision and goals across the organisation
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Inconsistent but improving company communications about the vision and goals. There are separate analytics visions for each business unit or a single corporate goal that is not communicated
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Company goals, vision and status are regularly communicated. Executives work towards formulating a shared analytics vision, understanding how each component works together
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Executives champion and promote the broader vision along with how their area contributes to that vision
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Communications channels are used to effectively update the internal organisation, their customers and the broader industry

question: If you have multiple business units, do they share a common vision for data and analytics?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no enterprise vision and minimal collaboration across departments
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: There is no enterprise vision but there is collaboration across departments
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There is a draft vision in place supported by most executives across most departments
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: There is a shared strategic vision.  Executives champion initiatives
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: There is shared strategic and operational vision that leads the industry

question: Is there a primary driver in your industry that is moving you toward a specific vision or capability?
Are there regulatory/compliance needs driving your organization’s priorities?
What are the business’s biggest challenges in getting the information they need from IT?
What are IT’s biggest challenges in providing the data and the tools needed by the business?
What are your strategic business initiatives for the next 12-18 months? What would the Executives say are the most pressing issues or challenges with analytics or data?
What needs or questions does your business have that is currently not able to be addressed with your existing analytics and data warehouse environment?
Who develops the overall data and analytics strategy?  Is there an analytic roadmap? If so, who is responsible for executing and updating the roadmap?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no broader business strategy for analytics and data
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A business strategy for analytics and data is emerging with a few key metrics defined
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A business strategy that has been defined and agreed for data and analytics
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A business strategy that shows analytics and data as a key part of the overall organisation strategy is in place and most metrics are defined
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The Analytics and Data strategy is a key differentiator and shows how the organisation uses analytics and data now and into the future

question: How are executives kept informed of priority projects and their status?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no project status reporting capability
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Project sponsors are updated monthly on their specific projects
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A company-wide program office provides weekly or monthly reports on the status of all analytics projects
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Some projects are delivered with project tracking tools that provide daily status updates and tracking
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A company-wide daily project status dashboard provides overview information with drill-down capabilities showing detailed project status based on project tracking tools

question: How involved are senior executives involved in the review and resolution of cross-functional issues? How are they involved in the prioritization and budgeting of projects? Is there an executive champion assigned to critical projects or programs?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no executive council or forum responsible for the vision, enterprise program or project execution. There are no standard processes for resolving cross-department conflicts
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: An Executive Council or Steering Committee has been formed to direct and oversee a critical project or program. An escalation process for resolution of critical issues is put in place
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: An Executive Steering committee regularly sets direction, resolves escalated program conflicts or issues and communicates updates
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: An Executive Steering Committee oversees direction and steers the analytics program for the company, promoting alignment and innovation
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: An Executive Steering Committee sets shared direction and champions projects leading to new insights

question: How are data and analytic needs reviewed, prioritized and budgeted?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Discovery is not treated separately from projects.  Executives not involved. Failures are covered up.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Analytics Discovery is funded as phase 1 of planned analytics projects
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Some discovery projects are funded at business unit level.  Executives embarrassed by failures
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Programmatic approach to discovery (e.g. A/B testing etc.) appears in some business units.  Executives of those units involved in prioritisation
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Organisation-wide adoption of analytics discovery with executives involved in both successes and failures.  Corporate-wide  prioritisation and funding controls

question: Is an approved business case required for analytics projects?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Inconsistent project prioritization and funding processes
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: High level discussions to prioritize and determine selected project funding
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Repeatable prioritisation and funding process with high level business cases
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Prioritization and funding processed work well and provide path for new ideas.  Business case defines and tracks metrics
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Prioritisation and funding promote operational improvements and strategic efforts.  Metrics effectively gathering and analysed to determine business case success

question: Describe the process for identifying and prioritizing projects.  Describe the criteria used when prioritizing (i.e. Complexity, Costs, Projected Benefits, Prerequisite Needs, Resource Needs, etc.). How far out does the planning go?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Inconsistent project prioritization and funding processes
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: High level discussions to prioritize and determine selected project funding
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Repeatable prioritization and funding process exists
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Prioritization and funding processes work well and provide path for operational improvements and new ideas
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Prioritization and funding promote discovery efforts, operational improvements and the strategic vision

question: Do all projects fall into this process, or are there different processes based on the project’s estimated cost, resource needs, or business function?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Little differentiation between how projects supporting operations and the strategic vision are funded or prioritized
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Business Cases are required for strategic or large value projects.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: All projects require business cases, with the level of detail appropriate for the size of the investment.  Different paths for approval for different project types (discovery, strategic, operational, improvement etc.) may start to appear
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Differentiated paths exist for discovery, operational and strategic projects.  All project types require some financial justification.  Creative funding ideas encourage continuous improvement.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Prioritization promotes and funds discovery projects quickly and differently from operational needs.  A consistent path exists for identifying and promoting strategic projects

question: How are potential projects estimated or qualified in preparation for the prioritization or funding process?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Estimates are prepared based on gut feel.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Prior historical outcomes are used to estimate value of new discovery projects
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Discovery projects are not estimated.  Operational and strategic projects are, based on historical proof points or estimated business value
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Discovery projects are not estimated.  Operational and strategic projects are, based on reliable financial modelling.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Discovery projects (e.g. A/B testing) are used to provide qualified estimates for larger projects

question: For those projects that do not qualify for prioritization and funding process, how are resources allocated and tracked? How does the business fund analytic discovery?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all non-project activities.  No value tracking is done for this time
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all non-project activities.  Effort is sometimes tracked and reported against task
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all non-project activities.  Effort is consistently tracked and reported against task assigned
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Investment pool is allocated to fund small analytics activities. Business value statements are submitted and reported for all non-project activities.  Resources are assigned to highest business value first
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Central pool of investment funds and resources exists for small project activity.  Resoucres are allocated based on business value which is tracked and reported on

question: What is your baseline for projecting data and analytic funding and resource demand? Do you start out with an annual budget that is driven by last year's budget (or example, plus or minus 5%)?  What is included in the funding of data and analytic initiatives (i.e. architecture, technology, business and IT resources, contractors, etc.)?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all non-project activities.  No value tracking is done for this time
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all non-project activities.  Effort is sometimes tracked and reported against task
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all non-project activities.  Effort is consistently tracked and reported against task assigned
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Investment pool is allocated to fund small analytics activities. Business value statements are submitted and reported for all non-project activities.  Resources are assigned to highest business value first
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Central pool of investment funds and resources exists for small project activity.  Resources are allocated based on business value which is tracked and reported on

question: Who is the final decision maker for funding and prioritization?   Is there an executive level position that provides input for data and analytic needs and priorities to the final decision maker?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: For larger projects, decisions to fund or proceed are made by a single sponsor
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Different business areas are starting to collaborate and partner when funding initiatives
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A standard prioritization process, shared by business and IT, exists.   Thresholds determine when a project or system request requires formal funding and prioritisation
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Prioritization and funding processes work well and provide path for operational improvements and new ideas.  Thresholds effectively promote discovert and completion of smaller projects whilst requiring estimating and design for projects with cross-organisational impacts
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Prioritization promotes and funds discovery projects quickly and differently from operational needs.  A consistent path exists for identifying and promoting strategic projects

question: Where in your organisation do Data Scientists sit?  Are they in departmental / line of business roles, or in IT, or in a central organisational structure?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are no Data Scientists
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data Scientists are in IT
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data Scientists are in line of business roles and no co-operation exists between groups
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data Scientists are in line of business groups but there is formal co-ordination and co-operation between groups
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Central pool of Data Scientists and some resources exists for small project activity.  Resources are allocated based on business value which is tracked and reported on

question: IIs there a pool of IT or analytic development resources shared across the business units? Are there different IT or analytic teams for applications and support?  (For example, are dataa & analytic teams organized to support specific tools or enterprise applications, like SAP?).  What about other cross functional teams, such as a BICC or a Data Management or Data Governance team?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all IT activities.  No value tracking is done for this time
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Annual headcount budget allocated to support.  Effort is sometimes tracked and reported against task
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Annual headcount budget allocated to cover all IT activities.  Effort is consistently tracked and reported against task assigned
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Investment pool is allocated to fund design and architecture of new projects. Business value statements are submitted and reported for all activities.  Resoures are assigned to highest business value first
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Central pool of investment funds and resources exists for small project activity.  Resoures are allocated based on business value which is tracked and reported on

question: How are corporate projects charged back to the business units?  Do you have charge-back mechanism for CPU usage, I/O, or data storage?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No Charge-back is done
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Charge-back is done based on overall system operational cost, split by the number of departments using the system
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Charge-back is done based on a basic IT metric such as CPU, # of users, or Storage space
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Charge-back partially done on the basis of all IT resources consumed, with separate metrics driving different cost bases
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Charge-back consistently done on the basis of all IT resources consumed, with separate metrics driving different cost bases

question: Are business cases required to allocate funded?  Are business cases initiated by the business or IT?  What criteria are required for a business case to be approved?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Estimates are prepared based on gut feel and generated by either business or IT.  No formal standards required.  No central lodgement and tracking
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Business Cases are standardised in requirements, but approved at business unit level inconsistently and neither centrally lodged nor tracked
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business Case submission and approval processes are standardised but slow.  Tracking is partial or incomplete.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Business Case submission and approval process is supported by process automation and can be done rapidly if required.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Business Case submission and approval process is supported by process automation and can be done rapidly if required.

question: How do you know when it is time to change your solutions or divest of the solutions you have? How do you balance investing and divesting? How is this planned for in your budget?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No end-of-life planning is done
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Funds are requested based on a case-by-case basis when assets fail or emergency replacements are required
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Systems with known end-of-life issues are planned to be replaced in the annual budget
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A systems review is conducted annually to determine which systems need replacement, based on a fixed pool of allocated funds
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A portfolio approach is used with funding assigned to cover discovery, deployment, improvements, operations and asset retirement

question: Who has the CAPEX and resource budget for IT? Who is the decision maker on data and analytic investment?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Analytics are funded from resource headcount rather than as projects.  IT owns the CAPEX and IT resource budget
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Analytics are funded by business sources.  IT owns the CAPEX and IT resource budget
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Analytics are funded from business sources.  IT owns a portion of the CAPEX budget for infrastructure but business can fund new IT capability as part of business cases
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Funds are distributed based on common agreement amongst business and IT executives on an annual basis.  Project funding is approved by business case
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Discovery analytics are separately funded.  General investment in split between IT for infrastructure and operations, and business for development of new capability

question: Are analytics, IT, or business oriented projects separately or independently funded?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: All projects funded using the same ad hoc process
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: All projects funded using the same structured process
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business and IT-driven projects are funded from separate sources.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Some or most IT projects are linked and funded together with a relevant business project that requires the capability
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Discovery projects are funded separately, whilst Business and IT projects are funded based on business strategy alignment

question: Do you have a long term roadmap that you follow that incorporates the major initiatives over the next few years?  If so, how is that managed?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no long term roadmap. Individual projects are approved independently and without strategic planning
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Major operational systems have long term roadmaps but analytics systems are not covered
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business and IT stakeholders come together to develop and approve a strategic program over at least 1 year timelines, including analytics systems
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Program Management effectively co-ordinates the execution of projects within a strategic roadmap covering operational and analytics systems
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Program management manages to a strategic vision but delivers in adaptable and agile ways to changing business needs

question: How are the milestones between different projects and initiatives coordinated?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Managing across projects or initiatives is difficult.  Projects often having competing needs and overlapping objectives
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A process of managing across projects has been defined for critical programs
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Program management standards and processes are leveraged to drive alignment and more effectively leverage resources across projects
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Proactive program management is done to keep related projects aligned and alert the team of other issues or changes that may impact program delivery
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The Program Management function is seen as best in the industry, regularly contributing to efficient business change

question: How does the organisation track value delivered from project investments?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No tracking is performed.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some larger projects are assessed for success, but little attention is paid from lessons learned.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Projects are regularly assessed for success and these lessons are incorporated into corporate memory and process improvements
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Smaller projects are performed faster and more regularly, providing early feedback onto project success and allowing failing projects to be terminated quickly
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Large initiatives are delivered in small chunks to allow for faster failure.  Smaller discovery initiatives are implemented to predict future value.

question: How are the ROI numbers in a business justification (e.g. Business Case)  estimated and vetted?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No ROI numbers are required
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: ROI numbers are estimated.  Larger projects are sometimes subjected to financial review of the ROI numbers by an independent team.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: ROI numbers are estimated for all projects.  A consistent set of parameters and values is used in all business cases. ROI numbers for larger projects are required to be independently vetted (e.g. by Finance or similar). s
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A consistent set of parameters and values (and sometimes a standard financial model) is used.  The estimated cost savings or revenue improvements are required to be adjusted in the sponsor's budget for the following year if the project is approved.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A consistent financial model for project ROI is used.  The financial model is improved on a regular basis to better predict outcomes.  Discovery projects are approved separately for blue-sky analytics concepts.

question: How does the organization monitor and measure the effectiveness (business value) of data and analytics to a business process?

Does each business case contain a measurement plan, which includes determining baseline metrics against which improvements can be projected (and presumably measured)?  How do you know if or when business case projections are achieved?  Is this something that is regularly measured after a project is implemented?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No tracking of results is done
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some projects contain measurement plans and are assessed by the Project Manager approx. 3-6 months after completion
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A corporate mandate for measurement plans and tracking results of business cases exists but it is incompletely complied with
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Measurement plans exist and tracking the results of business cases is done once at a specified point after project completion
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Measurement plans exist and tracking the results of business cases is automated and continuously updated.  Deployment methods allow for easy tracking of change

question: Describe the process of tracking and reporting on actual results. Are baseline metrics established consistent with the business case? Does the ROI analysis include projections of investment costs? Does the ROI analysis include projections of ongoing operating costs such as additional IT maintenance feed, new headcount, etc.?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No tracking of results is done
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: The project manager is responsible for results evaluation which is performed manually
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A central team (either corporately or per business unit) records the approved ROI metrics and collects data from the project manager to assess success
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A central team (either corporately or per business unit) records the approved ROI metrics and performs a monthly assessment of success to issue a report
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A central team (either corporately or per business unit) enters the approved ROI metrics into an automated system that tracks project outcomes daily

question: Do projects consider business and IT costs, needs and priorities?  Which ones get higher exposure/priority?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Business value is the only focus.  Costs are considered, but constraints are not.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Larger projects get executive attention but still do not consider constraints or non-financial measures
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business and IT costs are included, and some sense of resource constraints is sometimes included.  Senior executives approve all medium to large projects
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Resource and capacity constraints become commonly included in decision making.  Senior executives set thresholds and capacities, which are then applied by mid management for smaller projects
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Prioritisation in a scarce environment becomes the key driver for project prioritization.  Business and IT constraints include ability to train staff in new procedures, change management capacity and other factors are regularly considered

question: Are business cases for IT or other operational investments required?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No business cases are required for IT or operational investments
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Infrastructure investments are assessed in the same process as business-initiated changes
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Infrastructure investments are assessed separately to business-initiated change, within an assigned funding pool
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Business Cases for Infrastructure investments are required but assessed separately to business-initiated change
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A portfolio approach is used to balance funding across infrastructure, projects and discovery activities to enable all types of projects to progress.

question: Who is accountable for achievement of ROI goals? What corrective actions are taken if results fall short of projected goals?  Who is responsible for initiating and implementing the corrective actions?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No tracking of results is done
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: The project manager is responsible for the achievement of the ROI Goals.  No corrective actions are taken if the ROI is not delivered
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: The project sponsor is responsible for the achievement of the ROI goals.  A review is conducted if the ROI goals are not met.  Corrective actions are assigned to the Project Sponsor by the steering committee to resolve the issues
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: The project sponsor is responsible for the achievement of ROI, and a standards Post Implementation Review is conducted to learn for future projects.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: ROI achievement is consistently measured and used to assess management effectiveness

question: Are metrics common across projects, or specific to a single project? How are users educated about ROI, the metrics, and the process?
When and how is the business case process initiated?  What does the business case consider?
Do the business users have access to the data they need to complete their reporting and analysis?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Some required data not available for review or analysis
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data available for operational needs but only through transactional systems
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business has access to all operational data needed and some data for exploration or discovery
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data coverage includes all business functions and needs
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analytics dta avilable for all business functions and related needs

question: Have you considered the impact of “big data” on your data integration; e.g., are you able to link social media data to your Customer or Product master?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No "big data" is captured
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Big Data is maintained separately from operational data and cannot be integrated
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Ad hoc integration using approximation techniques are in place on an as-needs basis
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Specific matching keys (e.g. credit card or customer name) allow for moderate levels of matching
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Specific programs are in place (e.g. self registration, cookies, customer details matching) to increase the ability to link between Big Data sources and operational master data

question: How effective are the security and privacy management policies and processes of your organisation?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Security and Privacy polies are outdated or insufficient
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Security and privacy needs and regulartory requirements are understood and appropriate management is being initiated
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Security and privacy policies have been implemented to meet the security and regulatory requirements of the enterprise
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A comprehensive security management process is in place for the enterprise. Security and Privacy policies are solid, allowing easy access to those authorised, but preventing access to others
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: There is a continuous process improvement approach to security management with an understanding that data sources and types are continuously evolving

question: How often is data updated?  Are there certain data only available or updated daily or weekly?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data for analysis is updated on a daily basis and may be out of date when analysed
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data is kept current ofr targetted business needs though some challenges remain
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data currency is acceptable
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data is current for discovery and production purposes
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data is up to date with future predicted data effecively leveraged

question: Is the data in the analytics ecosystem of sufficient quality to meet most business analytics needs?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data Quality is not measured and is known to be poor
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: There are some data quality processes in place - usually manual and without data profiling
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data quality is acceptable, with data stewardship programs in place
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data quality is maintained and managed to standards and metrics
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data quality is effectively managed with meaningful metrics for accountability

question: How much historical data is immediately available (not archived) for online analysis?  Does the amount of online historical data support analysis requirements such as seasonal, current versus prior period, and period + 1 (13, 25, or 37 month) for trend identification?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Historical data is difficult to access
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some historical data is available
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Defined processes exist for sourcing and access to current and historical data
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Historical data is available for 1-2 years and archived (and recoverable) beyond that.  Sometimes summary historical data is always available.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Historical data is available for long periods of time but on slower response, lower cost platforms

question: Does your organisation have a defined information or data strategy.  Is that strategy capable of dealing with big data as well as traditional data sources?
Do you operate with an underlying principle that data is a corporate asset?  How is this manifested within the organization?
Do you have a planned sequence to load new sources of data?  Is this sequence well known and agreed by all parties?

Is there an information architecture and corresponding data model(s) that guides where each different type of data should be stored across a range of information and analytics platforms (e.g. IDW, Data Lake, Data Labs etc.)?  Are there data model(s) that allows for integration across analytics platforms?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: A consistent data model and/ or information architecture does not exist
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A draft information architecture and/or data model exists and is available to show high level data storage structrures and locations
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: An information architecture and/or data model is consistently leveraged when developing analytics or applications
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: An information architecture and/or data model is leveraged and referenced for consistency and to test the impact of new ideas
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: An information architecture and/or data model enables and supports current business needs whilst allowing the business to test new concepts and changing business needs

question: Can data and analytics users easily find out where data is stored and how it is structured?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: More time is spent finding and understanding and preparing data than in analysing it for business purposes
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data is consolidated into smaller numbers of data stores, but these are still not well documented
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A unified view of data is provided for most analytics purposes
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Metadata repositories provide users useful information on the location, structure and data quality concerns of most analytics data
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Analytics data is logically structured, located and organised and is supported by effective business-language search tools across platforms

question: Is data stored for analytics in a logically integrated manner, even if spread across multiple platforms?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data is acquired and integrated in a silo fashion by project or application or data mart
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data is acquired once and shared throughout the enterprise, eliminating some redundancy
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Management sees cross-functional information sharing as a way to scale up and prmoote enterprise-wide initiatives
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: The SDLC contains a process for addressing data management with an emphasis on acquiring data and integrating it using a standard approach
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Industry data interchange standards are in place facilitating data integration within the enterprise and with B2B partners.  Data assets are exploited across the enterprise

question: Is relational data stored in an integrated data model of some type?  What type?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data modelling is not consistently done
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data models exist for different business areas or functions
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A data model is available that represents the business
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data models are leveraged for consistency and used to test the impact of new ideas
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data models enable and support current business whilst allowing the business to test new concepts

question: Is non-relational multi-structured data stored in an organised, formatted, logical manner or stored in source format for later integration?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Non-relational data is not loaded
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Occassional use cases for multi-structured data are emerging but are handled as one-off projects without standards or integration
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A platform for multi-structured data exists but is not architecture or controlled
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Multi-structured data is organised and formatted in a logical manner but not integrated with other analytics data types
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data is integrated across the analytic ecosystem regardless of data type.  Employing loosely coupled or tightly coupled approaches appropriate to the data types and use cases

question: Can anyone load data into any analytic ecosystem, or only into data lab areas?  If anyone can load data anywhere, how is metadata captured and architectural control exerted?
How is reference and master data managed?  Is this centralised and shared, or maintained by individual systems

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is little consideration of reference or master data across the organisation
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some reference and master data domains are identified
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Reference and Master data is consistently defined with processes in place to ensure capture across applications
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Reference and Master data is manged consistently and in a consolidated way across the enterprise
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Reference and Master data enables and supports corporate changes

question: How do you define reference and master data within your major transactional applications?  Within your data warehouse, data marts, or data lakes?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is an application-centric approach to reference and master data.  Master data is not defined across the organisation
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Most applications and data repositories define master data locally, causing redundancy and reporting inconsistencies
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There is a clear vision for master data management that demonstrates how master data facilitiates strategic objectives
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: There is a formalized orgasniation associated with the Master Data program including defined roles and responsibilities, clearly defined metrics and an iterative learning cycle
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Reference and master data initiatives are taken in support of the strategic business initiatives and incorporated into the projects

question: What processes are in place to ensure reference data is consistent and that you have visibility to the changes made to various code values? Is this a manual or automated process?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Cross-business or cross-functional reporting requires master data reconciliation
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Cross-business or cross-functional reporting is completed with minimal reconciliation required for targetted reference and master data use cases
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There is foundational policy-driven standardization of technology and methods in place. Common usage of tools and procedures across projects
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Master data management is automated across systems with the business seeing the value of consistent foundational data

question: How would you describe the state of master data at your company?  How are master data updates communicated and managed across different functions?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is a lack of understanding how master data should be aligned to business initiatives
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Cross-business or cross-functional reporting is completed with minimal reconciliation required for targetted reference and master data use cases
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A formal master data management framework has been defined and is being implemented in all major systems
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Some domains have automated master data management in place, whilst others are managed manually.  Synchronisation across systems including analytics systems is standard
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Master data management is automated across systems with the business seeing the value of consistent foundational data

question: Are your existing data governance policies adequately addressing the naming standards necessary for successful master data management?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are no data governance processes in place for master data or reference data
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Governance processe are defined and implemented in enterprise systems
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Governance processes are defined to update master data
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Governance is effective with master data available and leveraged for discovery
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Governance processes are automated so that master data is effectively updated across systems and data repositories

question: Do you have data owners identified for your master data domains?
Have you considered the impact of “big data” on your master data; e.g., are you able to link social media data to your Customer or Product master?
Do you have enterprise business process workflows for each line of business involved in the data governance framework to maintain and approve master data?
Are the master data requirements for all major lines of business known? Are these master data items held in any centralized logical data model or repository?
Do you have a mechanism and rules in place to detect bad, inaccurate, or duplicate data? To what degree does your organization profile its master data?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data quality is an issue with lots of manual work-arounds
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Master data is up to date and consistent across the enterprise and the entire analytic ecosystem

question: Is there a set of MDM SLAs agreed on between the business and IT?
Does master data at your company undergo a structured and automated process to be corrected, cleansed, and approved?
Does the data warehouse act as a publisher for master data? In other words, is there bidirectional flow of master data between the operational systems and the data warehouse?
Do you store and track historical changes to your master data?
Do you have insight into the hierarchies and relationships between master data records?
Do you produce data quality metrics on your master data? How frequently are those metrics refreshed and reviewed by the governance committee?
Are the business rules related to your master data documented in the DW metadata repository?
How are changes in master data elements communicated and synchronized across the enterprise?
How does your organization ensure that different systems use data in the same manner and get the same results?

Is Metadata captured along with the data?  Is this business Metadata, operational or technical metadata?  What about data quality metadata? Is metadata specific to a data warehouse or to an analytics environment managed as part of a centralized solution, or do components of metadata exist across multiple platforms?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Metadata is captured occassionally as a part of an individual project or as part of a business glosssary
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some metadata is captured. Usually this is either system-specific or business metadata shown as a data dictionary or business glossary
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Metadata has been defined and collected for most data.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Metadta is effectively used and leveraged to enable user self-sufficiency in data access
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Metadata is leveraged to test and understand new ideas / concepts

question: Are data fields consistently defined across the organization?
Are you able to meet your regulatory requirements for data lineage, etc.?  Describe the challenges and barriers associated with doing so.
Describe the tools, processes, and techniques used to capture metadata information.   How is metadata defined and accessed across the systems?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Standards are not in place for metadata (e.g. no naming standards).  Metadata is usually manually maintained outside the application.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A metadata repostiory tool creates and maintains descrptions of data and can produce simply listings but they tend not to be user-friendly or useful
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: The methods and tools used to create common semantic definitions for business and IT terms, data models, data types and repositories are in place
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A metadata tool, with import and export abilities from other tools has been loaded and defined
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A repository is used to track near real-time updates as changes occur, providing alerts to targetted users based on rules

question: Who owns and manages metadata?  How do owners communicate changes or challenges?
What are you SMART goals, metrics, and KPI’s associated with metadata management?
How frequently is the metadata content refreshed?  What governance process is followed to standardize and harmonize metadata?
What is the governance process followed to add new metadata sources?  Is it based on business value or usage? Is it compliance driven?
Is there a single, standard tool and methodology for accessing the metadata?  Describe.

maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There may be different metadata tools requireing users to manually review and update metadata

question: How is metadata being used in the enterprise?  Examples could include data lineage, standardizing transformations, impact analysis, or audit and traceability.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Metadata is not used throughout the organization to aid development and user self-sufficiency.  Metadata is mostly obtained from talking to local SMEs
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: There are few secondary uses for metadata content
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Some tools or applications are starting to leverage available metadata
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Users can view data definitions, tehcnical transformations and samples of dat from tables when developing or updating queries, reports or analytics
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Users can view metadata and contribute observations and updates based on experience

question: Do data stewards or other data governance organizations establish and communicate metadata standards across the organization?

maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: The value of metadata has been discussed with critical metadata measured
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Metadata is valued and measured providing consistency across business functions

question: How do end users access definitions, transformation rules, and metric formulas?
Is Metadata seen as a valuable asset or a constraint?
What standards are being used while retrieving, transforming, and storing metadata?
Is there training available for end users and metadata developers?
Does your organisation make use of different data states and concepts, such as Data Lake, Data Warehouse, Master Data, Data Projection and Metadata across a variety of architectures and technologies?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data has no formal organisation or organisation defaults to past historical standards
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A draft data organisation strategy exists and is available to show high level data organisation definitions, patterns and the interactions between the different states and concepts.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A data organisation strategy is consistently leveraged when extending the capabilities of the Analytic Ecosystem
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A data organisation strategy is leveraged to test the impact of innovating and adopting emerging concepts and technologies
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A data organisation strategy  enables and supports current business needs whilst allowing innovation and adoption of emerging concetps and technologies

question: Does each data concept have a defined level of data governance?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No formal governance processes are practiced.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Governance processes are instantiated in silos of data and an integrated governance program is under development.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data governance processes are formally defined and practiced across major data assets of the organisation.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data governance processes are leveraged to test the impact of various levels of governance on achieving business goals within aggressive timeframes and the required level of accuracy.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data governance processes are largely automated and transparent allowing rapid exploitation of new data assets.

question: Does each data concept have a defined level of data integration?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Integration is only defined for mature data assets (e.g. Data Warehouse, Data Marts)
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Integration of data across the organisation is considered a key capability to achieve business advantages.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Integration of data assets is defined at an organisation level and is being leveraged to integrate data assets where required to achive the business outcome.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Integration of data assets is conferred through specific matching keys and allows for reasonable levels of integration.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Integration of data assets is conferred through specific matching keys, is largely automate and provides for full integration across master and event data.

question: Does each data concept have a defined level of data quality?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data Quality is not measured and is known to be poor
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: There are some data quality processes in place - usually manual and without data profiling
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data quality is acceptable, with data stewardship programs in place
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data quality is maintained and managed to standards and metrics
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data quality is effectively managed with meaningful metrics for accountability

question: How are data states organised across the different data concepts?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: States are duplicated across concepts resulting in multiple sources of truth (e.g. raw data is stored on multiple platforms for different purposes).
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some data states are common across the environment but as the data gets closer to business use duplication occurs.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A data organisation strategy is leveraged to minimise duplication of data states across the ecosystem and encourages re-use of data assets.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A data organisation strategy is leveraged to test the impact of rationalising data assets through efficient organisation of data states.

question: Does your organisation have a data lake? What is its main purpose?
Does your organisation have a data warehouse? Is it integrated?
Are the data lake and data warehouse integrated in any way. For example, the data lake may provide source data to the data warehouse for later integration.

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data is held in independent silos that do not interact with any other silo.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data virtualisation is used across the various data assets allowing seamless access to data regardless of physical location.

question: Do your data assets require a detailed level of definition to allow you to exploit the data asset?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Yes. Cannot use the data asset unless it is fully understood.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: The organisation is aware that all data has value at different levels of defintion and integration and is working towards a strategy to address this.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Different levels of definition and integration are applied to data assets according to a defined set of data centricity guidelines (e.g. data assets for exploration are loose/non- coupled).
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data centricity processes are largely automated and coupled with business and operational metadata allowing exploitation of data assets.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The business routinely is able to answer new business questions. Complexity of data assets in much reduced.

question: Do you data assets require a detailed level of defintion to provide value to the organisation?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Yes. Cannot use the data asset unless it is fully understood.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: The organisation is aware that all data has value at different levels of defintion and integration and is working towards a strategy to address this.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Different levels of definition and integration are applied to data assets according to a defined set of data centricity guidelines (e.g. data assets for exploration are loose/non- coupled).
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data centricity processes are largely automated and coupled with business and operational metadata allowing exploitation of data assets.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: The business routinely is able to answer new business questions. Complexity of data assets in much reduced.

question: Do you know what state of data you need to answer your business questions or perform the required analytics (e.g. source data, integrated data, summarised, etc)?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Minimal levels of refinement. Largely source like data with some integration.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Detailed definitions of Data Tiers have been established with the Data Warehouse and are being further revised to address data assets across the analytic ecosystem.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data assets are organised across defined Data Tiers that allow users to easily find the data in the state the require.

question: What different levels of refinement does your data pass through?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data is minimally refined or refined by the business user for consumption.

question: What level of sharing and reuseability is achieved with your data assets?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Silos. Not a lot of sharing.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data assets are routinely re-used. New data assets are quickly published and available for wide business use via standard interfaces (e.g. API)

question: Does  your organisation have a Discovery/Exploration data zone that allows you to explore the value of data without strict controls?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No discovery capability.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A strategy is being developed to provide discovery/exploration capabiliies.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data scientists and I.T. have access to a Discovery/Exploration zone.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: All the organisations data is accessible from the Discovery/Exploration zone and is used by Data Scientists and I.T. to find new business value.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: ??? Available to all???

question: Does your organisation have a process that allows new valuable data to be published into the operational are once the value of the data is proven?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No discovery capability.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A strategy is being developed to productionise newly discovered valueable data.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Newly discovered data assets are routinely productionised in a verifable and repeatable manner.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Newly discovered data assets are quickly productionised via automated procedures.

question: Does the company have a formal, published data security and privacy policy describing why customer data is collected, what the information is used for, who has access, and when it is deleted?
Is there an organizational function that is responsible for establishing the policies and auditing them to ensure compliance?  Where does that business unit fit within the organizational hierarchy?
Is there someone in the company with the official title of Head of Information Security or Chief Information Security Officer (CISO)?

maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There is a Chief Security Officer who sets the standards and monitors compliance

question: What are the regulations in your industry with which you are most concerned?  For example,GDPR or Sarbanes Oxley?
Is there a formal privacy policy that defines data privacy, access control, and auditing requirements specifically for data in the analytics ecosystem?

maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Security and privacy are proactively addressed with the inclusion of data security requirements in service level agreements and outsrouced contractual obligations
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data security is adddress within organisational initiatives (e.g. balanced scorecards, metrics frameworks, business cases etc.)

question: Does the privacy policy incorporate all standard privacy principles including: Accountability, Notice, Consent, Collection Limitation, Use Limitation, Disclosure, Access and Correction, Data Accuracy, Enforcement, and Openness?
Are there documented information security policies that govern data collection, storage, transmission, retention, and destruction?

Does your analytic ecosystem  contain PII, such as Social Security Numbers (SSN); Private Health Information (PHI); customer financial records (such as bank account details); credit card numbers (PAN), or other Non-Public Information (NPI)?  Are there procedures and techniques in place to mask or obfuscated this data?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no clear identification of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) throughout the enterprise and there is no catalogue of where that data is housed
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data has been appropriately classified and there is an inventory of applications that contain sensitive data.  Encryption techniques have been deployed to safeguard data
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: PII data has been secured through encryption and physical security has been addressed with access to mobile devices and portable storage devices.  Data security audits occur regularly.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Training is in place to promote security awareness and controls at all levels of the organisation.  There is an empahsis on the legal, contractual and regulatory requirements for data privacy and security
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: There is a continuous process improvement approach to securty management with an understanding that data types and sources are continuously evolving

question: Does the company have assigned data owners for all information assets who are actively involved in setting access policy, authorizing all access to their data, and regularly reviewing who has access to data in the analytic ecosystem?

Are the data owners aware of everyone who has access to their data and where all copies of their data exist?  For example, is data copied to spreadsheets and Access databases?  If so, are the same controls applied to this data?
Are data contained in the anlaytics ecosystem classified or identified according to a standard Data Classification scheme?

maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data has been appropriately classified and there is an inventory of whichh data types are in which systems

question: Does the company apply the principle of  least privilege when granting access to sensitive data?

Does the company use role-based access controls (RBAC) within the analytics ecosystem?  Are they leveraging organizational roles across the organization, or are they unique to the Teradata data warehouse?
Are they aware of all regulatory compliance requirements resulting from the types of data in the  EDW and the jurisdictions in which they operate?
Have they ever conducted a risk assessment or audit of the analytic ecosystem to determine compliance with company policy, privacy laws, and other regulatory compliance requirements?

How many users have direct ad-hoc query access to the analytic ecosystem?   Is access always granted from the access layer or do some users have access to the acquisition and integration layers (e.g., data scientists or ETL developers)?  How is that access managed across all environments – production, test, UAT, etc.?
How many external users or business partners have access to the analytic ecosystem?
Are  shared accounts used for accessing data in the analytics ecosystem that don’t provide accountability back to the originating end user?
Is there any logging of access to sensitive data?
Is there any process in place to monitor or review access log data?
Does the company use a formal or recognized information security management system (ISMS) framework, such as ISO 2700x, as a reference or benchmark for implemented security controls within the EDW?
Does the EDW support business-critical applications where system availability is important?
Are there any known risks regarding access to sensitive data that are not being adequately managed or mitigated?
How would you describe the overall quality of your data?  How does your organization handle data quality issues?  How are those issues identified and who is responsible for their resolution?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data Quality is not measured and is known to be poor
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: There are some data quality processes in place - usually manual and without data profiling
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Data quality is acceptable, with data stewardship programs in place
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data quality is maintained and managed to standards and metrics
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data quality is effectively managed with meaningful metrics for accountability

question: Are data quality feedback loops in place to report quality issues identifyied in the analytics ecosystem back to the operational system that is responsible for the creation of the bad data?
Is data quality measured and reported to the analytics ecosystem users at least daily so that they know if the data is of sufficient quality each day to support the analytics they plan to execute?
Is the data quality in the analytics ecosystem reported to senior management if it exceeds specified thresholds?
Are integration issues (where master data from one system doesn't not full match another) reported for resolution to a responsible person?
How much of your business leverages data for analytics today?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data is available for limited business areas or units
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data is available for all critical business areas
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business units have the majority of the data they need
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: All business units have the data coverage required for operations
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Business units have data for operational and strategic decisions

question: Is data available outside of functional applications?  (In other words, can business users access and explore data directly from an analytic ecosystem platform)
Are there business areas where there are gaps in data availability?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Not all functional areas have the breadth of data needed
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Critical functional areas have the breadth of data needed
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Functional areas have the data coverage needed for operations
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: There are no gaps in functional coverage
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data about data is gathered and available for new insights and predictions

question: Is some data stored in multiple repositories (data marts, data warehouses, etc.)?
Is data integrated across the organisation into a consistent coherent scheme?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data may be targetted for a specific group or need and may not be aligned to enterprise needs
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Critical enterprise-wide data is consistently covered to business users
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business areas and functions have consistent enterprise data for their use
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Proactive data coverage helps anticipate new data needs
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: New data is available for analytics the analytics and new predictions and forecasts are provided

question: What level of historical detail is retained online?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Historical data is difficult to access
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Some historical data is available
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Defined processes exist for sourcing and access to current and historical data
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Historical data is available for 1-2 years and archived (and recoverable) beyond that.  Sometimes summary historical data is always available.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Historical data is available for long periods of time but on slower response, lower cost platforms

question: Are prior periods summarised and retained online for analysis?
Do users frequently have to extract data from the analytics system(s) to merge it with other data that is not available on the analytics platform(s)
Application Section
Applications Section - Summary Questions
Does the business know which applications and tools to use to achieve the desired business analytics outcome? Are all desired business analytics outcomes supported by some form of technology?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: The business is often unable to achieve the desired business analytics outcomes as systems are either unavailable to them or there is no system for the given business function.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: A mapping of business functions and outcomes is available to guide the business in arranging access to the relevant system.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Businesses are guided by a comprehensive mapping of systems, their primary function and the data sets they contain to aid in determining which systems will be used to achieve the business analytics outcome.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Businesses are able to access a catalogue of available systems, business functions and data sets and select from the catalogue the data they need to achieve their desired business analytics outcome.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Business can explore and discover evolving information assets in order to exploit maximum business value.

question: When considering the analytics to address a business problem or use case, how do you know what data, or application to use? Are there different environments available for business users vs. I.T.?  Do Data Scientists have access to different analytic environments?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: I.T. prepare data in a format consumable by the specific application or tool that business department uses.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Standardisation of data delivery, applications and tools is underway to optimise the delivery of data for analytics.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Analytic environments are standardised across the organisation allowing rapid access to data.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: An Analytic Capability Roadmap guides I.T. and the Business across extensive analytic capabilities whilst exploring emerging trends.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Emerging analytic trends are monitored and tested to determine if additional business value can be gained from their adoption.

question: Are the business able to drive their business analytics outcomes with minimal assistance or do they require significant skilled support to achieve the business analytics outcome?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: The business relies on I.T. to provision all required data in its final format for business use.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: I.T. provides robust and productionised information and analytic systems to deliver business ready information assets used as-is.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: I.T. provides robust and productionised information and analytic systems to deliver business ready information assets.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Business departments are provided with the resources, tools and training they need to access existing information assets or to create new information assets for exploitation.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: As new data/information is captured in the organisation it becomes availability to business users for exploration and determination of business value.

question: Is the role of each analytics application well understood and clearly differentiated to other analytics applications, or is there substantial functional or data overlap?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are a number of systems in place without a clear understanding of how each adds value or delivers a specific business analytics outcome.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Systems are defined for critical business processes. Less critical business analytics outcomes are dealt with in an adhoc fashion.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A base Systems Architecture supports critical business processing.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Systems are engineered (through architecture) to optimise capabilities for critical business processes and outcomes.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Each system adds specific business value. The use and integration of systems enables industry leading performance and capability.

question: When considering analytics or advanced analytics, are you required to complete the analysis leveraging a specific application?  What happens if you have analytic needs that cross technologies or capabilities?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Analytics can only be carried on single platforms or systems. Data must be exported from one system to another where analytic needs cross platforms or data locations.
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Processes are being developed to allow cross platform analytic capabilities.
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Processes are in place to allow cross platform analytic capabilities.
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Technology solutions enable seamless cross platform analytic capabilities where required.

maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: A company-wide data owner is appointed and data stewardship and governance processes develop
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data is treated as a company asset with monitoring, measurement and improvement programs in place to improve the data value

question: Describe your organization’s approach to managing data.  Do you have a specialized governance team or set of roles within different groups in your organization responsible for defining and monitoring business data?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: Data is typically not integrated.  When integration occurs, it is for a specific purpose.  There is no data management role
maturity_descriptors.2_developing: Data for priority projects has been analysed for integration and re-use.  Emerging data management roles
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: As projects are prioritised, data is analysed to understand integration and re-use needs.  Data Management roles exist but are largely marginalised
maturity_descriptors.4_innovating: Data defined with integration and re-use in mind.  Data Management principles and practices are in place and standardised
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data is core to the business, with data integration and re-use built into business processes.  Data Management elevated to C-level

question: Is there a formal data management function within the organization?  Where does that function fall within the organization (e.g., within IT?  the architecture team)?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no data mangement function
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: An IT function is responsible for data management and co-opts business team members as required.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: A cross-functional team is accountable for data mangement and reports to senior business leaders.  Progress is measured, published and reviewed.

question: Are there documented principles, policies, procedures, etc. associated with data management?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are no processes in place
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There are generic policies and procedures in place
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data Management policies, procedures and practices are documented, shared, used and reviewed regularly for relelvance

question: Are there SMART goals associated with data management?  What are the metrics or KPI’s associated with your data management functions?  Are people rewarded for managing data as a corporate asset?  o  Are there incentives for data reuse within the organization?  Are there penalties for circumventing data management processes?   Are there documented expectations or service level agreements regarding data availability and quality

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are no goals for data mangement
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: There are defined targets for data mangement functions and these are regularly applied.  Data re-use is not tracked, but SLAs are in place
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data Management effectiviness is measured automatically and regularly. Data re-use is measured, reported and reviewed.  There are incentives in place to encourage complaince with data mangement principles

question: Do all teams access a central source for data, or are there different sources due to applications and/or different functional areas?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are no central data stores
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A significant core component of data is centrally sourced but local databases are also used for analytics in departmental silos
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Authorised analtyics staff can access the required data from across the organisation's systems.

question: How does your organization authorize personnel to leverage data?  Is this consistent across the organization? Are there specific roles set up for certain data?  Is there data that is available for all to review and leverage?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There are no or very limited authorisation or access controls in place
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: System-level access controls are in place to analytics systems.  Role-based security is in use.
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Field-level security is able to be implemented if reqiured.  Security logs are automatically scanned for exceptions.  Role, Group and level security allocations are available.

question: Is the data management function integrated within other business functions such as Strategic Planning, the PMO, etc.?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no data mangement function

question: Who represents the business for data subjects within analytics projects? For example, who attends information architecture sessions to provide consistent definitions of business concepts (for example, sales, claims, product, customer)?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no representation
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: Business SMEs are invited on a case by case basis to participate based on their domain knowledge
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Business SMEs, together with Data Stewards or other Data Management specialists or members of the BICC or equivalent, are routinely assigned to analtyics projects to provide business and data insight

question: Is there a single point of contact for identified data subjects/business concepts, or does IT have to reach out to multiple business users and personally take the responsibility to rationalize definitions?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: There is no clarity on data accountability
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: A Data Management function is in place to co-ordinate definitions and resolve data issues
maturity_descriptors.5_leading: Data Stewards are assigned to each data element and this information is readily available.  Clear definitions are in place for all key data items and reviewed reguarlary against current data usage and business needs

question: Is there a team of managers that is regularly involved in resolving escalated data issues?

maturity_descriptors.1_emerging: No
maturity_descriptors.3_practicing: IT managers discuss data issues on an as-needs basis
